title: Cheese Empanadas with Melting Mozzarella and Fontina
summary: Crimped, golden baked empanadas filled with molten mozzarella and fontina, soft onion, tender potato and a hint of chilli.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
ice-cold water, plus 1-2 tbsp if needed
large egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water, for glazing
medium onion, cut into 5 mm dice
small potato, peeled and cut into 5 mm dice
low-moisture mozzarella, cut into 5 mm cubes

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Blitz the flour, salt and chilled butter in short bursts in a food processor until sandy. With the egg and water whisked together, add them and pulse a few times more, just until the dough holds when squeezed; a spoonful or two of extra water helps only if it is crumbly. Shape it into a disc, wrap and give it at least 30 minutes in the fridge, which makes rolling much easier.

steps.title: Onion
steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a small frying pan over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, until soft and translucent but not browned. Slow cooking makes it sweet and mellow.

steps.title: Potato
steps.text: Cook the potato in a small pan of boiling unsalted water for 3-4 minutes, until just tender, then drain well. Dry potato will not make the filling wet.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Once the onion and potato are cool, mix them with both cheeses and the chilli flakes. Cool vegetables stop the cheese melting before it is wrapped.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Get the oven heating to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and cover 2 baking trays with paper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Dust the worktop with flour and roll the pastry to 2-3 mm, then cut 12 cm discs, rerolling the offcuts once to get 12. Heap about 2 tbsp of the cheese mixture on half of each disc, dampen the border, and fold the other half across. Squeeze out the air, pinch the edges shut and finish with a rope-style pleat or fork marks; any gap lets molten cheese escape.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the empanadas on the trays, brush with the egg glaze and bake for 18-22 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until golden. Rest for 5 minutes so the cheese is molten but not scalding, then serve.

tips: Leaking cheese is the most common problem; press out the air and seal and crimp each edge firmly.
Use low-moisture mozzarella, not fresh, which makes the filling watery.
For more heat, add a little more chilli flakes.
Eat them warm, when the cheese stretches.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat at 180 °C for 8-10 minutes, until hot through. Freeze unbaked for up to 2 months and bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
